findings.location: section 0, 'Contract hash' row (line 29); section 3 D-1 (line 51) and 'There is no other deviation' (line 54)
findings.claim: The composite identity extension is not purely mechanical. V2.4 adds a byte separator ('then LF, then the V5 blob id') that is not in the contract recipe it claims to extend. D-1 and line 54 still declare the extension mechanical and state there is no other deviation.
findings.evidence: V2.2 0.1 (line 40) says 'SHA-256 over the LF-normalized text of the V2.1 blob followed by the V2.2 blob, plus the V5 blob id'. V2.2 N-1 (line 449) has the same wording. V2.3 section 0 (line 37) says '... in that order, plus the V5 blob id', and V2.3 D-1 (line 130) extends only the blob list. V2.4 line 29 says '... in that order, then LF, then the V5 blob id'. The separator comes from BA-11 V1 §2 (a subordinate artifact), not from the contract. It changes the result: recomputed over blobs 6259a3be, fd7260c5, bc3d67a9 and 1919a32a plus f73157d9, the value is 74725e4d4bbf285b1dbaf0c53cdb428d9e143784d6433cc8771f97f66cd26d12 with the LF (equal to BA-11 V2 §4) and 4777c422b702e1b8b9af0eb4741c63ead0fcdfc466fc587f817e8f6492e482fd without it.
findings.required_fix: Either declare the separator as an explicit deviation (for example extend D-1: 'the byte-level reading of "plus" as LF followed by the V5 blob id is carried from the BA-11 hash procedure and fixes the recipe; it applies equally to the V2.3 composite') and correct line 54, or remove 'then LF' from V2.4 and leave the byte procedure to BA-11 §1. Do this before the Coordinator's textual verification of V2.4.

findings.location: section 0, 'Precedence' row (line 28) against the 'Contract hash' row (line 29)

findings.location: section 2 clause map (lines 38-45), BASE-15 row (line 42) and the absent NB-4 row
findings.claim: The clause map leaves ambiguous the baseline-closure wording for the inventory requirement, which is the exact subject of RC-C1. (a) The NB-4 blocker rows still say NB-4 closes on 'the completeness review', which read literally means the full review (REVIEWED). A baseline blocker would then be unclosable before implementation, so the RC-C1 contradiction persists in the blocker tables. (b) The BASE-15 row turns a requirement into a sufficiency statement and drops the 'agreed' condition.
findings.evidence: V2.1 line 1711: NB-4 '... the completeness review and the agreement are missing'. V2.2 line 467 and V2.3 line 147: NB-4 'open until the inventory, the completeness review and the corpus artifacts exist'. V2.4 does not map these rows. Line 45 only says blocker states stay as they are, and only V2.1 27.10's unchanged sentence 'NB-4 remains open until these baseline artifacts exist and are agreed' (line 1492) gives the right reading, by inference. V2.4 line 42: BASE-15 'satisfied, for the inventory part, by STATIC_REVIEWED'. BASE-15 (V2.1 line 1214) requires the procedure and corpus definition to be 'agreed', and the ruling text says only 'the baseline requires ... STATIC_REVIEWED' (a necessary condition).
findings.required_fix: Add a declared mechanical-consequence row, for example: 'NB-4 (V2.1 32/V2.2/V2.3 blocker tables): "the completeness review" reads as the design-time review yielding STATIC_REVIEWED (27.10 as amended); NB-4's state is unchanged'. Reword the BASE-15 row as 'for the inventory part requires STATIC_REVIEWED, with its review record agreed; REVIEWED is not a baseline requirement'. Declare both under section 3.

findings.location: section 2, V2.2 PA-11 row (line 41)
findings.claim: The PA-11 mapping leaves two normative readings open without flagging them for the Coordinator. (a) PA-11 says 'The review record is a baseline artifact', but after V2.4 there are two review outcomes. The REVIEWED record (produced after implementation, before LEARNING) and any class review reopened by the last sentence of the pre-approved text cannot be part of a baseline that is already sealed, unless a new baseline version and anchor follow (BA-11 V2 §2). (b) Condition 6 ('differences between the static and the dynamic source are resolved') is declared applicable to the design-time inventory, where no dynamic source exists.
findings.evidence: V2.2 line 332: 'The review record is a baseline artifact. Nothing in the inventory is called complete until it exists.' V2.4 line 41 remaps only the second sentence. BA-11 V2 line 37: 'change of a sealed artifact -> a new version ... new seal'. BA-06 V2 line 37 already applies its own reading of condition 6 (two blind static reviews compared), supported only by ruling item (10) ('compare inventories and resolve differences'), which V2.4 does not cite.
findings.required_fix: Do not reinterpret the pre-approved text. Add a declared note, for example: 'PA-11 "the review record is a baseline artifact" applies to the STATIC_REVIEWED record. The status and custody of the REVIEWED record, and of a reopened operation-class review, are not decided by V2.4 and need a ruling before the BA-06 candidate. For the design-time review, condition 6 is read as in phase-1 ruling item (10).'

Cite the ruling item that limits the review scope, or remove the '(Architect ruling)' attribution.

findings.location: section 9, last sentence (line 231)
findings.claim: BA-06 applies the V2.4 rule with an added qualifier that narrows it. V2.4 requires REVIEWED before the first LEARNING run of any kind; BA-06 requires it only for governing learning.
findings.evidence: V2.4 line 34 (pre-approved text): '... and that is required before the first LEARNING run'. BA-06 V2 line 231: 'Governing learning requires REVIEWED (V2.4).' V2.1 line 1098 defines NON_GOVERNING executions that include 'LEARNING runs when used as validation', and line 1373 makes LEARNING a run MODE. The qualifier therefore allows LEARNING-mode runs classified non-governing to happen before REVIEWED, which the ruling does not allow.
findings.required_fix: Replace the sentence with the V2.4 wording: 'The first LEARNING run (any governance classification) requires REVIEWED (V2.4).'

findings.location: Section 2, column DELIBERATE-VIOLATION SCENARIOS: rows S2 (line 23), S3 (line 24), E08 (line 25), E01 (line 30), E12C (line 42), E13 (line 45), E14 (line 50)
findings.claim: The deliberate-violation column is built mechanically as 'the control appears in CONTROL_CLASSES_EXERCISED and DELIBERATE_VIOLATION_FLAG = YES'. It does not use the control the scenario actually targets or the scenario's declared expected result. The rule is not stated in the artifact. As a result, many listed scenarios are not negative controls of the row's control, so the counts overstate negative-control coverage.
findings.evidence:
Recomputed from the JSON:
- S2/S3 (89 each): 40 of the 89 declare EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS 'S-2, S-3 no difference' with TARGET_NEGATIVE_CONTROL 'E-12 phase C and the declared residual'. Examples: WR-A-X5..X8, WR-B-X3, WR-SC-X6.
- E12C (82): 45 have TARGET_NEGATIVE_CONTROL 'S-2/S-3'. 10 declare the write is outside phase C: WR-{A,D,E,F,G}-X7 ('phase C ended at V1') and -X8 ('outside phase C'). WR-B-X0 declares 'phase B not adjudicated (NG-19b)'. V2.1 section 10.6 (lines 563-565) puts X0, X7 and X8 outside E-12 phase C adjudication.
- E08 (19): 15 are WR-G-* scenarios. Their target is S-2/S-3 or E-12 phase C, and their expected results never mention E-08.
- E01 and E13 list Q-I02 and Q-I04 as deliberate violations. These are group Q qualification scenarios (INSTRUMENT_QUALIFICATION, NOT_A_CONTROL). The same row says the control CANNOT_BE_DELIBERATELY_VIOLATED_IN_A_GOVERNING_RUN.
- E14 lists KS-SL1-POSTWRITE, KS-SL1-TX-MISMATCH and KS-SL4-NEG-DET. Their targets are 'KS (...)' and they never mention E-14. E-14 is recorded UNDER_CHARACTERIZATION only (V2.2 PA-4; registry: 'UNDER_CHARACTERIZATION only').
findings.required_fix:
- State the derivation rule in BA-02b.
- Build the violation column from the scenario's declared target control (TARGET_NEGATIVE_CONTROL, or an explicit per-scenario target-control field in BA-04) and require an expected control result that names that control's FAIL or detection.
- Move scenarios that only exercise a control as a secondary or residual channel to a separate 'secondary channel / residual' column.
- Move Q-I02 and Q-I04 into the E-01/E-13 no-violation reason as 'detection covered by qualification', not the violation column.
- Remove the violation list from E-14 (outside the predicate).
- Recount every row.

findings.location: Section 2 row E03 (line 32); summary line 53 ('Rows with state GAP or NEGATIVE_CONTROL_MISSING: 0')
findings.claim: E-03 LockHeld has no scenario that violates E-03 and no registered reason that it cannot be violated. The row is reported as COVERED_DRAFT, and line 53 declares zero NEGATIVE_CONTROL_MISSING.
findings.evidence:
- V2.1 section 5, PL row (line 459) defines the E-03 FAIL as 'lock not acquired or wrong mode'. The registry maps it to REFUSE, class A.
- The two listed 'violations', LK-LM1-CONFLICT and LK-LM2-CONFLICT (JSON line 3322 onward), hold the lock. They probe P-L5 exclusion on a non-protected scratch object and declare EXPECTED_PRODUCT_OUTCOME 'O3 SUCCESS' and EXPECTED_GROUP_VERDICT 'CANDIDATE_CHARACTERIZATION' ('P-L5 demonstrated or not'). They characterize LOCK_MODE candidates (V2.1 section 3.4); they are not an E-03 violation.
- No catalog scenario injects 'lock not acquired' or 'wrong mode at PL'.
- The condition can be injected, so the ruling's alternative 'sealed reason it cannot be violated' does not apply.
- The conflict probe does satisfy the V2.1 section 31 minimum-catalog item 'a conflicting writer probe', but not the Phase-1 BASELINE_READY negative-control rule.
findings.required_fix:
- Author in BA-04 a concrete E-03 negative control, for example NC-E03-WRONG-MODE / NC-E03-NOT-HELD: lock not acquired, or held in a mode other than the pinned LOCK_MODE at PL, leading to E-03 FAIL and a refused or aborted run. Its expectation would be SEALED_PENDING_PIN on the LOCK_MODE selection.
- Alternatively, record a reviewed reason why it cannot be violated.
- Until then, mark the E03 row NEGATIVE_CONTROL_MISSING and correct line 53.

findings.location: section 2 line 43 and 'Where' column; header lines 8-9, 12; section 6 conditions 3, 4 and 6 (lines 99-102); final block lines 145-147
findings.claim: The seal-time procedure cannot be carried out as written under BA-11 V2's byte-exact rules. (a) It does not say where the dated re-run (condition 3), the repeated post-I-57 reading (condition 4) and the SEALED state (condition 6) are recorded. If they are recorded in the artifact, the bytes change and the candidate and ratifications expire (BA-11 section 2); SEAL_HASH must equal CANDIDATE_HASH, so the sealed bytes can never read SEALED. (b) The trigger 'if any identity of section 2 changed, the candidate is re-prepared' is ambiguous. Section 2 includes commit SHAs ('Repository HEAD of the run: 1711112...', 'origin/main 1304101d997b'), and these have already changed: the artifact sits at d190ec09. A literal reading therefore triggers re-preparation before the candidate is even ruled on. The run's identity also disagrees with decisions section 210 and the phase-2 evidence README, which say the phase-2 read used an extract of origin/main 3375aadb. The blobs are identical, so there is no substantive effect.
findings.evidence: BA-11 V2 section 2 says 'any byte change after a candidate ruling: the candidate and any ratification expire' and 'RATIFIED -> SEALED: the artifact hash recomputed ... equals the CANDIDATE_HASH'. BA-03 line 99 says 'a re-run at sealing is required; if any identity of section 2 changed, the candidate is re-prepared'. git rev-parse gives HEAD = d190ec09 != 1711112. decisions I-52.md line 9183 reads 'Se leyó un extracto de origin/main 3375aadb', and the evidence README says 'against origin/main 3375aadb'. The four code blobs are identical at 3375aadb and 1304101d.
findings.required_fix: State normatively that: (1) the identity set for condition 3 is the ten (path, blob) pairs of section 2, resolved at the then-current branch HEAD (for the docs) and origin/main (for the code), and commit SHAs are informational only; (2) the seal-time re-run of the 32 checks (with date and resolved commits), the repeated post-I-57 reading and both ratifications are recorded outside the artifact bytes, in the ratification records and the BA-11 entry; (3) the authoritative BA-03 state is the BA-11 entry, and the in-file status fields are frozen at candidate time. Reconcile the recorded origin/main of the run with decisions section 210 and the README, or note explicitly that both commits carry identical blobs.

findings.location: PIN/STATUS/EVM_VERSION of 153 host scenarios; md section 2 (lines 26-31) and section 5 totals (line 52)
findings.claim: Most scenarios leave out evidence-derived values their expected results depend on, so their STATUS is wrong. The catalog breaks V2.1 26.2 ('an expected result that depends on an evidence-derived value is pinned to that value's version') and its own definitions of DRAFT and SEALED_PENDING_PIN_CANDIDATE.
findings.evidence: Every host run that goes past P0 needs E-04 PASS at P0 (V2.1 5; 3.3: PASS only if the observed tuple is in the admitted set). It also needs E-03 PASS at PL, where FAIL means 'wrong mode' and needs the selected LOCK_MODE; any entry FAIL or UNKNOWN gives O1 by 17.2 row 2. 153 host scenarios go past P0, but only the 8 CL-CLEAN runs pin both the E-04 admitted set and LOCK_MODE. 45 of the 153 are DRAFT with PIN NONE. The other 100 SEALED_PENDING_PIN_CANDIDATE scenarios (for example NC-S1-Y1 at JSON line 1961, WR-A-X0 at line 4019, EV-V-FX-2F at line 3905) pin only 'frozen EVM version'. Phase A fails closed without a model (V2.1 14; PA-2), yet 17 scenarios expect a committed outcome with EVM_VERSION = NONE: NC-E11M-PC (O7), EA2, PR-SOURCE-SWAP-MODIFY/DELETE, PW-CLONE-BASE/CASE/NESTED/SYMTAB, LK-LM1/2-PROPS/CONFLICT, E4-LEARN-R1, E4-VAL-R1, S1, PP and CL-CLEANUP-CHECK (all O3). Another 8 expect O2 after mutation with no EVM pin. BA-08 V2 section 11 rule 4 makes HOST_DEFAULT_MAP evidence-derived and pinned (SEALED_PENDING_PIN), and says that 'until pinned, the comparison of such an attribute is UNKNOWN (O5 path)'. No scenario pins HOST_DEFAULT_MAP, although every O3 or O4 expectation relies on S-1..S-3. BA-08 V2 section 10 also gives TOL_SCALE as 'UNSET — NO AUTHORITY', and the SL-R scale comparison depends on it.
findings.required_fix: For every scenario, derive the complete set of evidence-derived dependencies: E-04 admitted set (if it passes P0), LOCK_MODE (if it passes PL), frozen EVM (if it reaches MUTATION), HOST_DEFAULT_MAP and TOL_SCALE (if S-1, S-2 or S-3 decide the result). Record them in PIN and EVM_VERSION, reclassify STATUS, and recompute the md totals. Add HOST_DEFAULT_MAP, TOL_SCALE and the Architect rulings K-3, K-4 and K-6 (BA-08 V2) to md section 7 as prerequisites for sealing. A scenario whose result rests on TOL_SCALE cannot be declared until a TOL_SCALE authority exists (26.2).

findings.location: section 2, row SEALED_PENDING_PIN (line 29); BA-11 V2 section 2 and section 3.1 (line 68)
findings.claim: The SEALED_PENDING_PIN mechanism cannot work without breaking the seal. The pinned value is 'written' into a scenario that is already sealed, and no external pin record is defined.
findings.evidence: md line 29: 'sealed; the pinned value is written after it is frozen ... and before the first governing run'. BA-11 V2 section 2: 'any byte change after a candidate ruling: the candidate and any ratification expire'; a change to a sealed artifact is a new version, with a new registry and anchor. V2.3 1.3 condition 3 requires the hashes of 'the scenario expectations' to stay equal. BA-11 V2 section 3.1 lists only 'E-04 admitted set, LOCK_MODE choice' as pinned later: the frozen EVM and HOST_DEFAULT_MAP are missing, and no artifact or hash slot is named for pins.
findings.required_fix: Make each pin a named slot in the sealed scenario (for example PIN_SLOT = E04_ADMITTED_SET@R-1). Keep pinned values in a separate, hash-registered pin record: a BA-11 entry or a tuple field, with its own seal and anchor. State that writing a pin never changes the catalog bytes. List every pin kind (E-04, LOCK_MODE, EVM, HOST_DEFAULT_MAP) in BA-11.

findings.location: NC-S1-Y1 (line 1961), NC-E08-Y0 (line 2032), NC-E08-Y2 (line 2103): EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS and CONDITIONAL_EXPECTATION_RULE
findings.claim: The non-silent Y scenarios expect E-12 phase A to FAIL unconditionally. The G-1 ruling ('E-12 may observe it') and the catalog's own md 6.1 ('E-12 phase A may detect it too') do not support that.
findings.evidence: JSON: 'S-1 FAIL at PV; E-12 phase A FAIL (the injected write emits an unattributable event)', 'E-08 FAIL at PV; E-12 phase A FAIL ...', and CONDITIONAL_EXPECTATION_RULE = NONE. Whether the host delivers an event is not settled by any authority: V2.1 10.6 always says 'if the event is delivered'. If the event is not delivered, the run observes E-12 phase A PASS, which differs from the declared FAIL, so the group verdict cannot be PASS even though the target control worked.
findings.required_fix: Make the E-12 phase A result conditional, through a declared CER resolved offline from the sealed E-12 log of the same run (event delivered on the target handle => FAIL; not delivered => PASS). Keep the target-control result (S-1 or E-08 FAIL) and the abort unconditional.

findings.location: Q-I14-SILENT (line 581) PLAN_OR_INPUT; NC-E08-Y0-SILENT (line 2068) and NC-E08-Y2-SILENT (line 2139) CONDITIONAL_EXPECTATION_RULE

NC-E08-Y0-SILENT and NC-E08-Y2-SILENT are 'RUNNABLE only if Q-I14-SILENT recorded AVAILABLE at the coordinate' (Y0 or Y2). md line 35: 'a rule that the sealed evidence cannot resolve makes the scenario result UNKNOWN'. G-1 requires Wr-S availability to be measured, not assumed.
findings.required_fix: Extend Q-I14-SILENT (PLAN_OR_INPUT and EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS) to measure availability at Y0 and Y2, and at every coordinate used by a SILENT scenario.

findings.location: WR-A-X0 (line 4019), WR-D-X0, WR-E-X0, WR-F-X0 (line 5018), WR-G-X0: EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS and CONTROL_CLASSES_EXERCISED; BA-02b row E12C
findings.claim: The X0 scenarios expect E-12 phase C to be able to FAIL. X0 falls in the commit boundary (phase B), where events are only logged and never adjudicated, which is exactly what the authority these scenarios cite says.
findings.evidence: JSON: 'S-2 or S-3 difference; E-12 phase C FAIL as well if the event is delivered', with E12C in CONTROL_CLASSES_EXERCISED. V2.1 10.6, X0 row: 'boundary events are logged, not adjudicated (NG-19b)'. V2.1 9: the commit boundary runs from PV to V0 and its events are not adjudicated. V2.1 5: W-scan and phase C start at V0. WR-B-X0 states this correctly ('phase B not adjudicated'). BA-02b counts WR-A-X0 and the others as E-12 phase C deliberate-violation scenarios.
findings.required_fix: For X0 cells: E-12 phase C not applicable, the event is recorded in the phase-B log without adjudication, and E12C is removed from CONTROL_CLASSES_EXERCISED. Remove the phrase 'precedence over O7'. Remove the X0 cells from the E12C coverage in BA-02b.

findings.location: WR-G-X7 (line 5617), WR-F-X7 (line 5277); WR-G-X5 (line 5541), WR-G-X6, WR-G-X5-EV, WR-G-X6-EV (and WR-F-X5/X6 and their -EV variants): EXPECTED_PRODUCT_OUTCOME and CER
findings.claim: The tail and X7 expectations for writers that change a source or read-set object ignore the E-08 re-observation at PC. Under the authority that re-observation gives O7, not 'O3 with RESIDUAL_MISSED_CHANGE'.
findings.evidence: Proposal ALT-21D V2 E-08 table: the read-set 'is re-observed at PV and at PC and equals the PS observation ... ABORT (PV) / DIVERGENT or UNVERIFIED (PC)'. Proposal V3 3.2: the continuity set at PV and PC includes E-08. The V2.2 PA-1.2 and BA-02a registries both give E-08 as 'ABORT (PV) / divergent or unverified (PC)'. V2.1 17.2 row 7: a mandatory control that FAILs in CONT_PC gives O7. Wr-G modifies 'a source object or state of the read-set', so E-08 at PC detects it whether or not an event is delivered. The catalog nevertheless expects O3 residual at X7, and at X5 and X6 its rule says 'not delivered => O3'.
findings.required_fix: For Wr-G, and for Wr-F where the NOD entry is in the read-set, declare E-08 FAIL at PC and O7 at X5, X6 and X7. Where a phase-C event is also delivered, declare O7 with both channels. List E-08 at PC as a detection channel. Record that the 10.6 residual table does not apply to read-set writers, or ask for an Architect ruling if the intent differs.

findings.location: All 15 WR-F-* scenarios (for example WR-F-X1 at line 5055, WR-F-X7 at line 5277), fixture FX-2F

findings.location: LK-LM1-PROPS (line 3287), LK-LM1-CONFLICT (line 3322), LK-LM2-PROPS, LK-LM2-CONFLICT; E4-LEARN-R1 (line 3427)
findings.claim: Four problems. The LK scenarios use an invented group-verdict value. Their expected outcomes are not determined. E-03 has no deliberate-violation scenario with a determined result. E4-LEARN-R1 and LK-LM* each depend on a value the other is meant to produce.

V2.1 3.2 keeps E-01..E-13 fail-closed in every CHARACTERIZATION_RUN and gives no learning exemption.

Use only V2.1 1.3 verdict values. Add a concrete NC-E03 (for example lock released and re-acquired between PL and V1, or a wrong mode read back) with the E-03 result and outcome fixed by V2.1 3.4 and 5, and correct BA-02b.

findings.location: U-1 (line 7571), U-2 (line 7604), U-3, U-4, U-5 (line 7703), U-7, U-8, U-6b (line 7835): EXPECTED_PRODUCT_OUTCOME; md section 5 claim (line 52)

findings.claim: Ruling item 1 requires a concrete scenario that records E-14 and E-15 UNDER_CHARACTERIZATION. KS-KR-RECORD is not a concrete run, and the clean runs it relies on do not serve KR.

KS-KR-RECORD also uses 'PASS (EVIDENCE_COMPLETE)' for KR, which is a CONTROL group (PA-1.3); EVIDENCE_COMPLETE applies only to EVIDENCE groups (PA-3).

findings.location: CL-CLEANUP-INCOMPLETE (line 7968): EXPECTED_GROUP_VERDICT
findings.claim: A PASS group verdict is declared from a run that is INVALID by design, which the contract forbids.
findings.evidence: EXPECTED_GROUP_VERDICT 'PASS (EVIDENCE_COMPLETE; the run is classified INVALID as designed)'. V2.1 21.1.1: 'INVALID cannot support a PASS'. V2.1 1.3: INVALID means 'there is no governing run'. PA-3 condition 1 needs 'every required governing run of the group'.
findings.required_fix: Move the detection of an incomplete cleanup into a valid run, for example as an I-16 control-plane qualification negative control (Q-I16) whose own run stays governing, or obtain an Architect ruling that reconciles V2.1 31 (CL row) with 21.1.1. Do not declare PASS from an INVALID run.

findings.location: PR-SOURCE-SWAP-NEG-COPY (line 2644): EXPECTED_PRODUCT_OUTCOME and AUTHORITY_SOURCE_FOR_EXPECTED_RESULT
findings.claim: O2 cites 17.2 row 3, but that row's condition is not met, and V2.1 19.1 and V2.2 PA-6 point to O1. The catalog settles a contract ambiguity by itself instead of escalating it.
findings.evidence: The scenario modifies the copy 'between acquisition and the first import'; the import 'does not start', so nothing is written. 17.2 row 3 requires 'TM = NOT_OPENED after a PREPARE-W write'. 19.1 prose says 'a mismatch stops the import: O2 with the residue produced so far'. The 19.1 UNKNOWN row ('the copy hash differs from the record') together with PA-6 ('the acquisition is UNKNOWN and the run is refused (O1)') gives O1. Row 2 is 'before any product write'.
findings.required_fix: Either move the copy modification to just before a second import, after a completed PREPARE-W write, so that row 3 applies unambiguously, or request an Architect ruling on a copy mismatch before the first import (O1 or O2). Until then, do not declare O2.

findings.location: PR-SOURCE-SWAP-MODIFY (line 2574), PR-SOURCE-SWAP-DELETE (line 2609), PW-CLONE-BASE (line 2714), PW-CLONE-CASE (line 2750): FIXTURE FX-1F
findings.claim: These scenarios use FX-1F, which already contains every required library block. No import happens, so the acceptance criteria of SOURCE_SWAP_CONTROL and CLONE_NON_REPLACE_CONTROL are never exercised.
findings.evidence: BA-08 V2 section 12 (Templates): each fixture contains 'the source rack drawn by the exact build, the required library blocks as imported by that drawing'. FX-IMP exists precisely for 'a template in which a block required by the mirrored plan is absent'. V2.1 4.3.1 SOURCE_SWAP_CONTROL: 'PREPARE-W then runs the import ... the imported definitions equal the content of the private copy'. CLONE_NON_REPLACE_CONTROL: 'the import runs under DuplicateRecordCloning.Ignore'. The catalog itself writes 'import (if any)'. PR-SOURCE-SWAP-MODIFY and -DELETE are also flagged DELIBERATE_VIOLATION_FLAG = YES with expected control results 'every control PASS'.
findings.required_fix: Use FX-IMP, or an FX-IMP-based L-VAR variant, for SOURCE_SWAP_CONTROL (modify and delete) and for CLONE_NON_REPLACE_CONTROL BASE, so that an import binds to the pre-existing homonyms. Set the deliberate-violation flag and target consistently with a PASS expectation.

findings.location: NC-E11M-PV (line 1751), NC-E11M-PC (line 1786), AB-AFTER-MUTATION (line 3106), NC-E12A (line 1821), NC-WU-FOREIGN (line 1926), KS-SL1-TX-MISMATCH (line 3178), NC-E10 (line 1716): EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS
findings.claim: Expected control results list only the target control. The authority fixes other results in the same runs, and the catalog has no rule for controls it does not list.
findings.evidence: A canary assembly load changes the E-10 managed-assembly snapshot (V2.1 12.1). E-10 at PV and PC must equal the baseline (12.3), so E-10 must also FAIL in NC-E11M-PV, NC-E11M-PC and AB-AFTER-MUTATION; only E-11M is declared. NC-E12A injects at Y1 'an operation ... on an object of the phase-A domain' without naming it; per BA-08 V2 section 5 that domain is source, NOD, containers and created objects, so S-1 or E-08 would also FAIL. KS-SL1-TX-MISMATCH (a non-top transaction) is likely to change the E-06 count. NC-WU-FOREIGN also makes the E-10 baseline fail. For NC-E10, 'before the P0 baseline snapshots' does not say whether the load comes before or after the subscription (13.1 step 4); after it, E-11M also refuses. V2.1 26.1 requires 'per control: PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN'.
findings.required_fix: Add a normative default for unlisted controls (for example 'every unlisted control PASS'). Declare every collateral result the authority determines (E-10 FAIL at PV and PC for canary loads, and so on). Make NC-E12A concrete: name an object and operation that neither S-1 nor E-08 observes, or declare those results. Pin the NC-E10 injection to a single step of 13.1.

findings.location: md section 1 schema (lines 20-21); section 3 (line 35); the 89 SC-A and SC-B scenarios; EA2-DEFERRED-EVENTS (line 2209)
findings.claim: Three fields required by V2.1 26.1 are missing: PURPOSE, INJECTIONS (writer identity) and EXPECTED_EVENTS / EXPECTED_DETECTION_CHANNEL. Many conditional expectations are written without a CER, contrary to md section 3.
findings.evidence: The 89 scan scenarios declare 'PASS if the observed outcome and channel equal the declared expectation', but no field declares the channel (SEMANTIC_COMPARISON, E-12, BOTH or NEITHER). 51 scenarios carry conditional text in EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS (for example 'E-12 phase C FAIL as well if the event is delivered') and 64 in EXPECTED_GROUP_VERDICT (EA1, EA2, WR, WU), all with CONDITIONAL_EXPECTATION_RULE = NONE. EA2 expects O3 unconditionally, but its verdict is conditional; if A-2 is false, a phase-C event on a protected object gives O7 (17.2 row 7).
findings.required_fix: Add PURPOSE, INJECTIONS (writer, variant, position) and EXPECTED_DETECTION_CHANNEL, with a per-phase EXPECTED_EVENTS, to the schema and to every scenario. Move every conditional expectation into a CER that states its offline resolution source; make the EA2 product outcome conditional.

findings.location: EV-L-OP01..EV-L-COMPOSED (for example EV-L-OP02 at line 3531, EV-L-OP03-04 at line 3565): PLAN_OR_INPUT
findings.claim: The learning micro-scenarios refer to operation classes that do not exist in the document they cite. They also merge classes that BA-06 V2 split, and one class has no micro-scenario.

BA-06 V2 3.3 defines only OC-BT-OPEN, OC-BTR-NESTED, OC-BTR-VIEW, OC-REF-PIECE, OC-DYN, OC-REF-ARRAY, OC-LAYER, OC-TEXT, OC-DIM, OC-ENVELOPE, OC-IMPORT, OC-REF-TOP and OC-VERIFY-READ. BA-06 V2 section 9 says the 'V1 labels OPxx map to the classes of 3.3' but gives no mapping. D-02 split V1 OP-02 into OC-BTR-NESTED and OC-BTR-VIEW, yet EV-L-OP02 keeps them together. EV-L-OP03-04 merges V1 OP-03 (nested placement, OC-REF-ARRAY) with OP-04 (OC-REF-PIECE), against 27.2 step 2 ('each operation category is executed in isolation'). OC-VERIFY-READ has no micro-scenario (27.2 step 1: 'No primitive may be used that has no micro-scenario').
findings.required_fix: Rename and re-author E12-L as one micro-scenario per BA-06 V2 3.3 class, using OC-* identifiers, with separate micro-scenarios for OC-BTR-NESTED and OC-BTR-VIEW and for OC-REF-ARRAY and OC-REF-PIECE, and add OC-VERIFY-READ (or record why it is excluded). Publish the mapping table in BA-06.

findings.location: REPETITION of the CL-CLEAN-* scenarios; md section 7 row C-3 (line 354)
findings.claim: No scenario uses PARAM-03, the clean-run sample for measuring the false-rejection rate. This measurement is required and is an Owner Act 2 input.

V2.1 26.3 defines CL-CLEAN as clean runs for 'control evaluation, false-rejection measurement'. V2.1 10.6 requires baseline runs without writers to measure the false terminal failure rate, and V2.1 24 item 3 lists it for Act 2. BA-10 V2 defines PARAM-03 (Owner question Q-O4). md C-3 lists only PARAM-01 and PARAM-02 with Q-O1..Q-O3.

findings.location: Q-FPSPEC-VECTORS (line 647): TUPLE_REQUIREMENTS; OU-* (for example line 2244), U-6, AB-COMMIT-EXCEPTION-T1
findings.claim: The CONTROL_PLANE_TUPLE of Q-FPSPEC-VECTORS does not bind the artifacts under test. The synthetic OU tuples do not bind the contract version whose 17.2 table they reproduce.
findings.evidence: Q-FPSPEC-VECTORS uses 'control-plane source SHA, evaluator assembly SHA-256, evaluator version, synthetic log fixture hash'. It tests the I-12 fingerprint provider against the BA-05 vectors: it has no evaluator and no synthetic log (INPUT_STATUS = NO_PLAN_INPUT_REQUIRED), and it binds neither the provider assembly, nor FINGERPRINT_SPEC_VERSION and hash (a tuple field per V2.1 28 and 2.1), nor the vectors file hash. The OU tuples leave out the contract composite hash, although the predicate and the evaluator rows are bound to the contract version (V2.1 1.7, EXEC-10).
findings.required_fix: Give Q-FPSPEC-VECTORS its own tuple: provider assembly SHA-256, FPSPEC version and hash, vectors file hash, and control-plane SHA. Add the contract composite hash (BA-11 V2 section 4) and the scenario catalog hash to CONTROL_PLANE_TUPLE.

findings.location: NC-E12D (line 1856)
findings.claim: A governing refusal (O1) is declared for a failed subscription. V2.1 21.1 treats an interrupted subscription as INVALID, and the G-2 ruling's list of runtime refusals does not include E-12.
findings.evidence: V2.1 21.1: a GOVERNING run needs 'all required subscriptions intact for the whole run', and 'lost subscription' makes the run INVALID. V2.1 14 and the registry say 'subscription failure at P0 | refuse'. G-2 lists 'E-02..E-07, E-09, E-10, E-11M' as runtime controls that refuse; E-12 is not among them.
findings.required_fix: Cite a ruling that a subscribe failure at P0 is a runtime refusal and not the 21.1 'lost subscription', or request one. Apply the same treatment to any E-11M subscription-failure scenario.

findings.location: INPUT_STATUS of the 10 FX-IMP scenarios and of fixture-variant scenarios (PW-CLONE-CASE, PW-CLONE-WRONG-TYPE, NC-E07, PW-CLONE-NESTED, PW-CLONE-SYMTAB); md 6.4 (line 339)
findings.claim: INPUT_STATUS 'FIXTURE_SPEC_DEFINED' claims more than BA-08 V2 section 12 specifies.

The variants used (a homonym that differs only by case; a layout, anonymous or xref record carrying the required name, which is also three alternatives rather than one plan; an unresolved xref in the read-set; T-IMP with nested blocks or symbol records present) are not among the fixtures in BA-08 V2 section 12.

findings.location: NC-S1-Y1, NC-E08-Y0 and NC-E08-Y2 (and the -SILENT variants): EXPECTED_PRODUCT_OUTCOME
findings.claim: The ruling's 'O2 if abort verify matches' became an unconditional O2. An ABORT-VERIFY mismatch (O6) would then count against S-1 or E-08 instead of S-5.
findings.evidence: G-1: 'S-1 at Y1 => ... O2 if abort verify matches'. md line 320 keeps 'when ABORT-VERIFY matches'. The JSON states 'O2 (abort before Commit; ABORT-VERIFY match ...)' with CER = NONE.
findings.required_fix: Add a CER resolved from the sealed ABORT-VERIFY record (match => O2; mismatch or unreadable => O6, recorded as an S-5 / AB finding), as already done for PW-IMPORT-PARTIAL-FAIL.

findings.location: NC-E04-R2 (line 1891) PIN; E4-VAL-R1
findings.claim: Deriving the admitted set that NC-E04-R2 is pinned to is circular under V2.1 3.3.
findings.evidence: V2.1 3.3: a value enters the admitted set only if observed 'in every governing run of the designated route(s) and in no governing run that violates the envelope'. NC-E04-R2 is such an envelope-violating governing run, yet its own expectation is pinned to that admitted set. md section 2 requires pins never to come 'from this scenario's own outcome'.
findings.required_fix: State the exact derivation source of the E-04 pin (E4-LEARN-R1, plus a non-governing R-2 characterization if exclusions are needed). State the order of runs, and that governing negative-control runs never feed the pin.

findings.location: The SC-B X7 set (WR-A/D/E/F/G-X7 only); E-11M and E-12 phase C negative-control classes
findings.claim: Some scenario classes required by the contract's coverage rules are missing.
findings.evidence: V2.1 10.8: 'group SC-B includes an X7 scenario per writer'; there is no Wr-B or Wr-C at X7. V2.1 31 (E-11M row): 'loss of subscription detected'; no host scenario exists (Q-I09 only qualifies the instrument). V2.2 PA-1.4 names NC-E12C as a required class for E12-V; the catalog maps phase C only to the WR-* scenarios.
findings.required_fix: Add WR-B-X7 and WR-C-X7 (or record why Wr-B and Wr-C collapse to Wr-A at X7). Add an E-11M subscription-loss scenario, or a sealed reason why it cannot exist. Either add NC-E12C or record in BA-02b that the WR cells discharge it.

findings.location: CONTROL_CLASSES_EXERCISED (all scenarios); MODE of the host-less synthetic scenarios; NOTE field; EXPECTED_GROUP_VERDICT of E4-LEARN-R1 and PR-CLOSURE-COMPLETENESS; EXPECTED_LOG_RECORD_SET default (md line 41); SC-B CER source
findings.claim: Several fields are internally inconsistent or do not follow their definitions in the contract.
findings.evidence: (a) CONTROL_CLASSES_EXERCISED holds control keys (S1, E08, WUM...), but V2.1 26.1 and 31 check 3 require registry classes. The clean runs serve PR-REC, PR-FRESH and PW without listing S5REC, S5CLO, LIBF or S5MAN, and BA-02b shows '(none)' clean scenarios for them. (b) OU, U-6 and Q-FPSPEC-VECTORS use MODE CHARACTERIZATION_RUN, which V2.1 3.2 defines as 'one catalog scenario in one AutoCAD process'. (c) NOTE is not in the md section 1 schema. (d) EVIDENCE_COMPLETE is used in CONTROL groups (E4, PR-REC); PA-3 limits it to EVIDENCE groups. (e) The default EXPECTED_LOG_RECORD_SET ('record types of the phases the scenario reaches') gives no counts (26.1) and is read from the run itself. (f) The SC-B CER decides 'delivered' from the log of E-12, the control under test, so a class-B E-12 miss (10.6) cannot be told apart from non-delivery.
findings.required_fix: Rename the field to CONTROLS_EXERCISED and add a CLASS column, or map keys to classes. Align GROUPS_SERVED with the controls listed and with BA-02b. Define a mode or a MODE note for synthetic runs. Add NOTE to the schema. Use CONTROL-group verdicts. Declare record types and counts per scenario. Name an independent delivery witness (the writer's own record, or the I-14 qualification at that position) in the SC-B CERs.

findings.location: PR-SOURCE-SWAP-MODIFY, PR-SOURCE-SWAP-DELETE, PR-TORN-READ; md 6.2 (line 326)
findings.claim: These scenarios deliberately change the original library file, which is a BUILD_BOUND tuple field. By the catalog's own G-2 table any tuple-field mismatch makes the run INVALID, and the catalog does not say when the tuple's library hash is sampled.
findings.evidence: V2.1 2.1: 'block-library file path and SHA-256 | BUILD_BOUND'. md 6.2: 'governed tuple identity mismatch (any field of V2.1 2.1 differs from the baseline, whatever its origin) | the run is INVALID'. The scenarios modify or delete that file after acquisition, or during acquisition for PR-TORN-READ.
findings.required_fix: State that the tuple library field is sampled once, before acquisition, and that the swap intended by 4.3.1 is not a tuple mismatch (citing the authority). Require the original file to be restored before the next run's tuple check, as part of cleanup.

findings.location: Section 2.1 line 31 vs section 2.2 line 52; vectors EV-12 (line 102) and EV-17 (line 107); contract V2.1 section 28.1 line 1513
findings.claim: The normative field order inside a record is contradictory. Section 2.1 streams fields 'in the schema order of section 2.3', but section 2.2 (and the governing V2.1 28.1: 'property keys inside a record are in sorted ordinal order') says property keys inside a record are 'sorted, ordinal'. The normative vectors pin the unsorted schema order.
findings.evidence: EV-12 streams 'name=...\nlayer=~' although 'layer' < 'name' ordinally. EV-17 streams 'label=...\ninner={...}' although 'inner' < 'label'. The DEFINITION_DUMP and ENTITY field lists in 2.3 are not sorted either. An I-12 implementer following V2.1 28.1 or BA-05 2.2 literally would sort fields and fail EV-12/EV-17. BA-05 declares no deviation from V2.1 28.1.
findings.required_fix: Resolve it normatively. Either (a) define 'property keys' in 2.2 as the keys of map-valued fields only (dynamicProperties, overrides, SYMBOL_RECORD property maps), state that record fields follow the section 2.3 schema order, and record this as an interpretation of V2.1 28.1 for Architect ruling; or (b) sort record fields ordinally and regenerate every vector. Add a vector that discriminates the chosen rule.

findings.location: Header line 7; section 2.3 line 63; section 2.5 lines 75-79; section 5 lines 167 and 169 step (4)
findings.claim: The census-to-seal sequence contradicts the versioning rule. Section 5 requires the library census before this artifact (FPSPEC-V1) is sealed. Sections 2.3/2.5 say a census type is UNKNOWN until 'a new version of this specification' adds its property list, and that adding a type is a change of the baseline. Either V1 is sealed without the census types, so every closure holding them (library blocks almost surely hold LINE/LWPOLYLINE/ARC etc.) is UNKNOWN and every governing run is O1. Or the spec is re-versioned before seal, which changes the 'FPSPEC-V1|EXACT|' domain separator and every normative digest in the JSON.
findings.evidence: Line 63: 'property lists are fixed by the census, one new version of this specification when the list is added; until then such a type is UNKNOWN'. Line 79: 'adding a type is a new version of this specification (and a change of the baseline)'. Line 167: 'The census is required before this artifact is sealed'. Every vector stream starts with 'FPSPEC-V1|EXACT|'. It is also unclear whether 'new version' means ARTIFACT_VERSION (n-DRAFT) or FINGERPRINT_SPEC_VERSION (the tuple field and domain separator).
findings.required_fix: State explicitly that before seal the census property lists are added to the DRAFT of FPSPEC-V1 (new ARTIFACT_VERSION, same FINGERPRINT_SPEC_VERSION, vectors unchanged), and that 'new FINGERPRINT_SPEC_VERSION / new baseline' applies only to additions after seal. Say which version field changes in each case, and adjust census step (4) to match.

findings.location: Section 2.3 lines 56-67 (DEFINITION_DUMP, ENTITY, BLOCK_REFERENCE, ROTATED_DIMENSION, SYMBOL_RECORD, NOD_ENTRY, ENUMERATION); section 2.1 line 31 conformance statement
findings.claim: The production record schemas are not byte-determinate. The value-kind encodings are exact, but the mapping from production records to value kinds is not specified. Two I-12 implementations can each reproduce all 18 digest vectors and still produce different digests, or lossy ones, for the same drawing state.
findings.evidence: (1) No field has a declared value kind: scaling, units, annotative (a 3-state enum), colorSource, colorValue, lineweight, transparency, horizontalMode and verticalMode could each be int, enum-string or bool. (2) dynamicProperties and overrides are 'set of (name, value)', but no pair/tuple kind exists in the 2.1 table or in enc_value, and the values are heterogeneous. (3) DEFINITION_DUMP says the nested digest is 'carried with a reference encoding', but BLOCK_REFERENCE lists only 'blockName' (a string) and no digest field. (4) It is not stated how ENTITY and its concrete type compose in the stream (one record? which record-type name inside '{...}'?). (5) SYMBOL_RECORD gives no field names for text style/linetype, and dimension style is 'the full variable set'. Registered applications, part of the V2.1 11.3 closure, have no entry and so are UNKNOWN under 2.5, while BA-08 V2 section 6 requires SYMBOL_RECORD of 'the dimension style in effect' and the regapp name set in every run. (6) NOD_ENTRY 'value (canonical)' and ENUMERATION handle encoding / per-container order are undefined. (7) No vector exercises any production record type except PAYLOAD_EXACT; EV vectors use undeclared TEST_* record types (V1 declared TEST_COORD3/TEST_NAME; V2 does not).
findings.required_fix: Give every production record type a field table with name, value kind and encoding. Define a pair/map encoding, the BLOCK_REFERENCE nested-digest field, the ENTITY+concrete composition, the SYMBOL_RECORD field lists per table (including dimension-style variables and regapp), NOD_ENTRY canonical value and ENUMERATION element encoding. Declare the TEST_* record schemas as test-only and exempt from 2.5. Add at least one normative vector per production record type.

findings.location: Section 2.3 line 65 (PAYLOAD_EXACT); section 1 line 22; EV-19/EV-20 lines 109-110
findings.claim: PAYLOAD_EXACT is defined as 'the raw stored bytes ... concatenated chunk by chunk', but the payload is not stored as bytes. The mapping is ambiguous (which character encoding?) and lossy (chunk boundaries and type codes are dropped). Differently stored Xrecords get equal digests, contradicting the layer-1 claim 'equal digests = equal state' used for S-5 and E-08.
findings.evidence: RackBlockData.cs:18,35-39 (main 3375aadb) stores a ResultBuffer of TypedValue(DxfCode.Text, string) chunks of 255 UTF-16 chars; Read (lines 80-86) concatenates only Text entries and ignores others. The spec does not say UTF-8 vs UTF-16, whether to encode per chunk or after concatenation (per-chunk UTF-8 breaks on a surrogate pair split at a 255-char boundary), whether type codes or chunk boundaries are part of state, how non-Text TypedValues are handled, or how a missing payload is represented.
findings.required_fix: Define PAYLOAD_EXACT over the stored ResultBuffer: an ordered sequence of (typeCode int, value encoded by its kind), preserving chunk boundaries and non-Text entries. Optionally add a separate derived field for the concatenated JSON as UTF-8 of the concatenated string. Define absent-payload encoding. Correct the wording ('raw stored bytes') and regenerate EV-19/EV-20 accordingly.

findings.location: Section 2.3 line 63 and section 2.5 lines 75-79; section 5 procedure; interaction with BA-08 V2 section 6 line 87
findings.claim: The only way to add an entity type is the library census, but RackCad itself draws types outside section 2.3 in RackCad-owned definitions of other kinds. Those types can never enter through a library census. BA-08 V2 section 6 puts 'DEFINITION_DUMP of every RackCad-owned definition' in the abort read-set, so any drawing that also holds such a definition would be refused (O1) with no path to fix it. This is not disclosed.
findings.evidence: RackCantileverCommands.cs:151-158 writes the RACKCAD_SELECTIVE payload on a definition built by CantileverViewMaterializer, which adds Circle (line 237) and Polyline (line 255). StructuralSectionMaterializer.cs:103 adds Polyline. Otherwise explicitly declare the resulting O1 refusal as a disclosed availability cost.

findings.location: Section 2.1 line 38 (string) and line 42 (unordered set); section 2.2 lines 51-52; EV-15/EV-16
findings.claim: Two string rules are underspecified for a .NET implementation. The ordinal sort basis: 2.1 says UTF-8 byte order, but 2.2 and V2.1 28.1 say only 'ordinal', which .NET StringComparer.Ordinal implements as UTF-16 code-unit order, and the two differ. Ill-formed UTF-16 (lone surrogates): .NET Encoding.UTF8 silently substitutes U+FFFD, so distinct stored strings collide in the exact layer; the Python reference encoder raises instead of returning UNKNOWN.
findings.evidence: In-memory check: U+FF21 vs U+1F600 sort as [FF21, 1F600] by UTF-8 bytes but [1F600, FF21] by UTF-16 code units. EV-15/16 use only 'a','b', so they cannot tell UTF-8, UTF-16 or culture-sensitive order apart ('B' vs 'a' would). enc_value calls v.encode('utf-8') with no Unknown path.
findings.required_fix: State in 2.2 that ordinal means UTF-8 byte order (not UTF-16 or culture order). State that a string that is not well-formed UTF-16 yields UNKNOWN. Add vectors with a case-mixed set and a BMP-above-surrogates vs supplementary set, and an UNKNOWN vector for a lone surrogate; make the encoder raise Unknown for it.

findings.location: BA-05 V2 section 2.7 line 87; JSON 'stream' fields; gen.py lines 74-75
findings.claim: Section 2.7 says 'the JSON file is authoritative for the exact bytes', but the JSON does not hold the exact bytes. It holds a display form in which LF is rendered as the two characters backslash+n. That form is ambiguous whenever content contains a literal backslash+n, and show() cannot represent non-UTF-8 raw bytes (the B kind).
findings.evidence: The current 18 streams happen to contain no other backslash, so they are recoverable today. A future vector with a JSON escape, a Windows path or arbitrary raw bytes would be ambiguous or would crash show() (b.decode('utf-8')).
findings.required_fix: Add an exact field per vector (for example 'streamHex' or 'streamBase64') produced by gen.py and declare it authoritative. Keep 'stream' as informative display only, or escape backslashes in the display form.

findings.location: Section 3.3 lines 142-152 (SV-01..SV-09); section 3.1 lines 122-123; BA-04 V2 Q-FPSPEC-VECTORS
findings.claim: The 'NORMATIVE semantic comparison vectors' are partly prose and cannot be reproduced mechanically, as Q-FPSPEC-VECTORS requires ('every semantic verdict reproduced'). The comparator predicate is also not pinned.
findings.evidence: SV-04 ('unknown member nested inside a known sub-object ...', persisted 'any'), SV-05 ('coordinate y = +0.0'), SV-06/07 ('length 10.0 in', no record type or field), SV-08 and SV-09 are prose. SV-01..03 use a literal "ExtensionData" JSON key, but RackEmbedDocument's [JsonExtensionData] is flattened on the wire (as EV-20 correctly shows with 'futureMember' at top level), so the two representations disagree. Not pinned: inclusive vs strict comparison (GeometryTolerance.AreClose uses <=); per-component vs Euclidean distance for points (Vector2D.ApproxEquals is per-component, V17 LN-3 uses distance); the canonical 'exact numbers' form of PA-8 rule 1 (1 vs 1.0). SV-09's 'refuses the run (O1)' describes the layer-1 PREPARE-R closure, not a semantic comparison, which is post-write (O5 path).
findings.required_fix: Give each SV vector concrete typed inputs (record type, field, exact values or wire bytes) and state whether the columns are wire form or typed form. Pin the predicate (|a-b| <= tol, per component or by distance per value class) and the canonical number rule of PA-8 with vectors. Reword SV-09 to the layer-2 consequence, or move the O1 note to 2.5.

findings.location: s6.2 step 3 (line 94); s9 steps 1 and 6-7 (lines 142, 147-148); s10 row 'whole log rewritten' (line 173)
findings.claim: The verification algorithm compares the CURRENT head entryHash with the anchored head. The procedure itself always appends an entry after the anchor, so every honest log fails verification (or the check gets ignored).
findings.evidence: Step 1 anchors MANIFEST_CUSTODY_HEADER_HASH = entryHash of the head (genesis, index 0). Step 6 then appends an ANCHORED entry holding the commit SHA and tag object id. That entry cannot be inside the anchored commit, and step 7 defers it to the next evidence commit, where another ANCHORED entry is appended again. So the head never equals the anchored head, and 6.2 step 3 always reports 'the log changed after the anchor'. The anchor record already carries CUSTODY_LOG_HEAD_INDEX (line 143), but verification does not use it. (V2.1 29.4 has the same wording; BA-07 is the operational procedure and has to be workable.)
findings.required_fix: Rewrite 6.2 step 3 and the s10 row. Compare the entry at the anchored CUSTODY_LOG_HEAD_INDEX with MANIFEST_CUSTODY_HEADER_HASH. Treat entries after the last anchored index as pending re-anchor, and state which events may legally sit there (at least the ANCHORED entry that records that anchor). Require each pending entry to be covered by the next anchor (step 7).

findings.location: s2.1 PARAM-01 row (line 29); s2.2 PARAM-01 (lines 37-47); memo Q-O1/Q-O2 (lines 100-101) and cost note (line 106)

findings.location: header BASE ITEM (line 12); s1 third rule (line 20); PARAM-04 row and method (lines 32, 68); PARAM-05 row and label (lines 33, 76); memo Q-O5 (line 104)
findings.claim: There is an unresolved sequencing conflict. V2.1 21.7 and 22 (BASE-18) require every MUST_FIX value to be fixed before the authority baseline. BA-10 makes the PARAM-04 value depend on host dry-run evidence, defers the PARAM-05 label value to manifest capture (EXEC-11), and states a weaker general sealing rule ('before the first governing run').
findings.evidence: V2.1 21.7: MAX_ATTEMPTS and machine-class label = MUST_FIX_BEFORE_AUTHORITY_BASELINE. V2.1 2.1: machine identity class is a 'recorded label agreed at baseline'. BA-10 line 68: the PARAM-04 value 'stays UNSET until the dry-run evidence exists (host work, not authorized)'. Dry runs need the implemented control plane and seams (EXEC-2/EXEC-3) and host authorization. BA-10 line 33/76: the label 'is assigned at capture' (EXEC-11). BA-10 line 20: 'sealed before the first governing run'. BA-11 V2 row BA-10 lists DEPENDS_ON only 'BA-01, Owner decisions Q-O1..Q-O5' and omits the dry-run evidence. As written, BASELINE_READY implicitly requires implementation plus authorized host dry runs, which nothing declares. This is the same kind of contradiction RC-C1 resolved for the operation inventory.
findings.required_fix: Get an explicit Architect/Coordinator ruling, or a pre-approved contract micro-errata, on one of two readings. Reading 1: the baseline fixes the method or policy (PARAM-04 method and beta; PARAM-05 label rule), and the value is pinned before the first governing run under a SEALED_PENDING_PIN-like rule. Reading 2: BASELINE_READY depends on authorized non-governing host dry runs. Then make BA-10 section 1, the header, and BA-11 DEPENDS_ON consistent with that reading.

findings.location: s2.1 PARAM-02 row (line 30); s2.2 PARAM-01/02 text (lines 37, 45)
findings.claim: PARAM-02 applies a per-run zero-failure formula to a failure mode defined between runs, without a reference, so N_det can be off by one. The independence premise is asserted rather than declared as an assumption.
findings.evidence: The mode is 'the event multiset of a plan differs across runs' / 'a non-identical ... multiset for the same plan'. Non-identity is a pairwise property. If the reference is the first run of the N_det, only N_det - 1 runs can reveal a deviation, so N_det = 1 + ceil(ln(alpha_det)/ln(1-p_det)). The formula holds as written only if each run is compared with a fixed reference such as the frozen EVM f(plan). Line 37 derives independence from 'each a fresh process'. A fresh process does not make systematic modes (machine, fixture, host state) statistically independent.
findings.required_fix: Define the per-run event of PARAM-02 against a fixed reference (the frozen EVM expected set), or add the +1 reference run. Declare independence as a modelling assumption of PARAM-01/02 and disclose it.

findings.location: s2.2 PARAM-04 (line 68)
findings.claim: The PARAM-04 method introduces an unregistered parameter (beta), uses a point estimate that degenerates, and leaves the accounting of attempts incomplete.
findings.evidence: 'a Coordinator-chosen engineering bound beta' is not listed as UNSET with its owner in s2.1. m = smallest m with r^m <= beta uses the observed rate r directly: if the dry runs show 0 INVALID, m = 1 (no retry at all), and a small sample understates r. An upper confidence bound on r, as PARAM-03 uses, would be robust. Contamination causes are excluded from r, but the text does not say whether contamination-caused INVALID attempts consume MAX_ATTEMPTS.
findings.required_fix: Register beta as an UNSET Coordinator value with its intent. Base m on an upper confidence bound of r by cause. State whether contamination-caused attempts count toward MAX_ATTEMPTS.

findings.location: s2.2 PARAM-05 proposal table (lines 74-77)
findings.claim: The proposed machine-class policy is internally inconsistent and mixes tuple classes.
findings.evidence: Line 77: 'change of any attribute = a new machine class'. Line 76: the label is 'MC-<first 12 hex of SHA-256(MachineGuid)>'. Two classes that differ only in OS build, AutoCAD build, profile or SECURELOAD/TRUSTEDPATHS would therefore carry the same label. Line 75 also puts the AutoCAD build and acad.exe SHA-256 into the class, but V2.1 2.1 classifies them as BUILD_BOUND, not MACHINE_PROFILE_BOUND.

findings.location: section 3, row SL-5 (line 38); section 6, row BlockLibraryDatabaseCache (line 60)
findings.claim: The warm-up imports 'from the private library copy Database', and 'the mirror path does not use' BlockLibraryDatabaseCache.
findings.evidence: The per-run authoritative private copy and the LibraryInputRecord are made in PREPARE-R inside the governed window (V2.1 19.1 steps 1-6; step 5: any cache entry is keyed by the copy hash and a generation id 'incremented at every fill'). PA-5 conditions 6 and 7 forbid the warm-up from mutating the LibraryInputRecord or changing the generation id. V2.1 section 6 also puts 'AUTH-12 presence queries' in PREPARE-R, and the V2.1 preamble records that 'the external one reads the process-cached library database'. At main that query goes through BlockLibraryDatabaseCache.Acquire (AutoCadExternalLibraryBlockQuery.cs:27). No artifact forbids that query on the mirror path, so the non-use claim is unsupported.
findings.required_fix: Specify that the warm-up library access uses a warm-up-only copy and Database, never entered into the run cache or LibraryInputRecord, and disposed before step 4. Add a normative rule, in BA-08 V2 or BA-06 V2, that the mirror PREPARE-R does not call the external AUTH-12 query and the process cache. If it may, treat BlockLibraryDatabaseCache as governed-window state: record its key and Database identity in the boundary record and the residual.

findings.location: section 4, rows SL-Y (line 69) and SL-P (line 71); section 12, Templates (line 158); fixtures FX-ANN and FX-DIM (lines 153-154)
findings.claim: SL-Y ('layers added by the seam') is covered by CL-CLEAN-FXANN-FP, CL-CLEAN-FXANN-LAY-FP and CL-CLEAN-FXDIM-FP. 'Every class has at least one concrete draft scenario.'
findings.evidence: Every template must contain 'the source rack drawn by the exact build'. With FX-ANN or FX-DIM toggles, drawing the source runs LateralHeaderDrawer.AppendInstance/AppendDimension, which creates RACKCAD_ANOTACIONES (LHD:270, 330-331) and RACKCAD_COTAS (LHD:356). The source's own DBText and dimensions then keep those layers in use. BA-04 V2 CL-CLEAN-FXANN-FP says 'RACKCAD_ANOTACIONES absent in the template' and CL-CLEAN-FXDIM-FP says 'RACKCAD_COTAS absent'. Both cannot be built from the template rule, so the seam never adds a layer and the 'created' case of SH-ANN cannot be reached. Similarly, every fixture has 'no RACKCAD_PROJECT NOD entry', so the SL-P element and the WR-F 'change a NOD entry the kind consumes' target are undefined unless 'consumed ABSENT' is stated.
findings.required_fix: Either specify a template construction in which the RACKCAD layers are absent while the source rack is valid (and show that it does not violate L-29/L-33), or record SL-Y 'added' as a case that cannot occur for a mirror of a product-drawn rack, with a sealed reason, and correct the coverage table and BA-04 V2. For SL-P, define the element as the consumed registry state including ABSENT, and define WR-F as the ABSENT-to-present change.

findings.location: section 11 ORACLE_SPEC, Inputs (line 134) and rule 2 Independence (line 139)
findings.claim: The oracle 'shares only immutable plan data types', and its inputs (including the plan) are 'captured and sealed at PV, before Commit()'.
findings.evidence: HeaderBlockInstance has public setters for every member plus a mutable Dictionary<string,double> DynamicParameters (Application/Drawing/HeaderBlockInstance.cs:57-101). HeaderRunPlan and HeaderGroup expose the caller's lists as IReadOnlyList without copying (HeaderRunPlan.cs:15-19, 107-112). The seams (LateralHeaderDrawer, or AUTH-15 overload A) receive the same object graph during T_M. PV comes after the writes, so an expectation taken from the plan at PV is not independent of what the writer did. A T0 guard that checks the oracle references no writer type does not prevent the writer from mutating shared plan objects.
findings.required_fix: Correct the fact: the plan types are mutable. Require the oracle input to be a deep, canonical, hashed capture of the plan taken in PREPARE-R before any seam call, sealed then, with PV only checking the sealed hash. Add a check that the plan the seam received equals the sealed capture.

findings.location: section 11 ORACLE_SPEC, rule 1 (line 138)
findings.claim: The oracle derives each expected element 'from those inputs only': SL-R 'from the transform and the plan layer', SL-Y 'from the plan (layer names and colours)', and SL-D/SL-N texts and dimensions from the plan.
findings.evidence: HeaderRunPlan and HeaderBlockInstance carry no layer names, colours or top-level layer (verified members). The layer names and ACI colours are private writer constants (LateralHeaderDrawer.cs:324, 327, 331 ACI 2, 356 ACI 1). Other writer rules decide the persisted form: default text height 3.0 when TextHeight <= 0 (:268); centre/mid alignment plus AdjustAlignment (:273-280); dimension rotation from |dy| <= |dx| and the dimension-line position (:345-349); named style if present, else db.Dimstyle plus 8 DIMVAR overrides (:353-373, 380-392). 'The plan layer' for SL-R is not among the listed inputs. As written, the oracle must either copy writer code, which breaks rule 2, or is incomplete.
findings.required_fix: Fix these writer-behaviour rules in ORACLE_SPEC as independent specification constants, citing the code facts: layer names and colours, text defaults and alignment, the dimension geometry rule, the style choice and DIMVAR overrides. Add the source of the top-level reference layer (the I-52 authority) to the inputs, and state how plan parameters that the block does not expose are expected, since the writer silently ignores them (B3 F23).

findings.location: section 12 Fixtures (lines 146-158)
findings.claim: 'All fixtures satisfy the consolidated clean values of evidence B4 (table 2)', and the fixtures are 'parameterized specifications' giving 'only the differences from the clean values'.
findings.evidence: B4 table 2 sets DepthCount=1, NumberFronts/NumberLevels/DrawRackName=false and Dimensions=0 ('Avoids L-11, L-22 ... L-30'). FX-2F, FX-4F, FX-BIG (DepthCount 2, 4, 3), FX-ANN (texts on) and FX-DIM (dimensions on) break those values, so the sentence contradicts the table. Parameters that change the plan and the names are not fixed: FX-2F and FX-4F give no bay count, levels per bay, BeamId or rack name. The rack name drives the definition names and the envelope Name, and AUTH-15 at 3375aadb refuses a blank envelope Name (RackDefinitionCreator.cs:177-183). L-VAR is not parameterized, yet BA-04 uses it both for homonyms with different content (PW-CLONE-BASE) and for a proxy entity in a required block (PR-REC-CLOSURE-UNKNOWN), which would also make PW-CLONE-BASE refuse. FX-BIG 'above learning' cannot be checked while the learning fixtures' quantities are open. BA-04 marks all of these, including FX-IMP (K-8 open), as FIXTURE_SPEC_DEFINED.
findings.required_fix: Give every fixture a full parameter vector: rack name, bays, levels per bay, BeamId, DrawBasePlate, toggles, DepthCount and separators. State per fixture which B4 clean values are deliberately overridden and which V17 limitations remain avoided. Parameterize L-VAR, split into separate variants if needed. Mark FX-IMP as specification-open (not DEFINED) until K-8 is ruled.

Add to the symbol-record list every layer the created entities land on (resolved through HOST_DEFAULT_MAP and PRE_COMMAND_STATE_RECORD) and the transitive records of the dimension and text styles in effect.

findings.location: section 8, 'Delivery in a governing run (finding PH2-E4-1)' (line 113)
findings.claim: R-1 must be delivered by the governed control plane 'as keystrokes to the command line (allowed automation)', and Q-ROUTE-R1 checks the 'R-1 signature (no script, LISP, DDE or transparent bit)'.
findings.evidence: V2.1 21.5 lists the allowed automation as 'the governed control plane (launcher, script-driven in-process harness commands, supervisor)'. It lists as contamination 'any other process interacting with the governed AutoCAD process (automation, message injection, ...)'. Keystroke injection into acad.exe is not among the listed forms and looks like message injection. The one in-process mechanism the contract does name (script-driven) is R-3, which BA-08 makes UNSUPPORTED (AUTH-15 run3 used run.scr). The 'R-1 signature' is an absence of CMDACTIVE bits, which does not tell R-1 apart from R-2, R-5 or R-6, whereas V2.1 3.3 D-4 requires the route to be 'recorded, not inferred'.
findings.required_fix: Do not label keystroke delivery 'allowed automation'. State the conflict with 21.5 and send it to the Coordinator and Architect (K-5/K-6) as an open question, either ruling keystroke delivery by the control plane as allowed or designating an in-process route with an amendment. Define how D-4 is recorded by the delivering control plane, and do not present the bit pattern as the route identity.

The V2.1 10.6 expectation table (lines 563-565) puts X7, X0 and X8 outside phase-C adjudication. V2.1 section 31 goes further and classifies the WR-*-X7 tail-log scenarios as NOT_A_CONTROL. The finding understates this: WR-{A,D,E,F,G}-X0 are also counted as E12C violations, although V2.1 10.6 says boundary events at X0 are logged, not adjudicated.

**E08 (19).** Only NC-E08-Y0, -Y0-SILENT, -Y2 and -Y2-SILENT target E-08. The other 15 are WR-G-* (9 plain plus 6 -EV). Their target is S-2/S-3 or E-12 phase C, and their expected control results never mention E-08.

**E01/E13.** Q-I02 and Q-I04 are group Q instrument-qualification scenarios; V2.1 section 31 classifies that group as NOT_A_CONTROL. Their TARGET_NEGATIVE_CONTROL is instrument acceptance ("pointing at a different file gives a mismatch"; "an unreadable variable gives UNKNOWN"). Ruling G-2 wanted qualification to appear as detection coverage inside the no-violation reason, not as a violation.

**E14.** The three KS scenarios have targets "KS (failure typing / TransactionMismatch / InvalidTransform)". V2.2 PA-4 and V2.2 section 31 record E-14 as UNDER_CHARACTERIZATION only, outside the predicate. Listing deliberate violations for it contradicts the row's own reason, OUTSIDE_THE_PREDICATE.

**Severity: MAJOR.** No row flips to GAP today: S2/S3, E08 and E12C each still have some scenarios that target them, and E01/E13 have the reason column. It does not reach BLOCKING, because BA-02b is DRAFT and already blocked by NB-2. But the column is the evidence for design-level coverage check 2 (V2.1 section 31) and the Architect's BASELINE_READY rule. As built it:
- overstates negative-control coverage by roughly half;
- contradicts the contract's own TARGET_NEGATIVE_CONTROL definition and its X7 = NOT_A_CONTROL classification;
- hides that E12C's genuine violation scenarios are all conditional (X5/X6/ABA). The NC-E12C class required by V2.1 section 31 and V2.2 PA-1.4 is absent from the catalog.

The required fix is sound: state the derivation rule, and derive the column from TARGET_NEGATIVE_CONTROL plus an expected result that names the control's FAIL or detection. Move secondary and residual channels to their own column, move Q-I02 and Q-I04 into the no-violation reason, drop the E-14 violation list, and recount every row. The X0 scenarios should also come out of E12C.

I checked this myself at d190ec09. BA-02b section 2 (lines 20-51) does not state how the DELIBERATE-VIOLATION column is built. Every count matches: S2 89, S3 89, E12C 82, E08 19, E01 [Q-I02], E13 [Q-I04], E14 [the 3 KS scenarios], E06 4, E12A 4, E11M 3.    - BA-04 V2 section 6.1 says X0..X8 belong to the W-scan experiment (all after Commit), and that "Negative controls of S-1 and E-08 need coordinates **before PV**" (Y0/Y2).

- `INJECTIONS` ("writers (10.6) and positions, or none");
- `EXPECTED_EVENTS` / `EXPECTED_DETECTION_CHANNEL` ("for scan scenarios: semantic comparison, E-12, both, neither").

None of V2.2, V2.3 or V2.4 removes or renames these fields. V2.2 PA-3 only adds `EXPECTED_PROCEDURAL_RESULT`. The Phase-1 ruling item (8) also does not waive them.

The BA-04 V2 md schema (section 1, lines 20-21) leaves out all three. A python scan of the JSON found the same: 29 fields present in all 217 scenarios, `NOTE` in 15, and zero occurrences of `PURPOSE`, `INJECTIONS`, `EXPECTED_EVENTS` or `EXPECTED_DETECTION_CHANNEL`.

The writer identity survives only as free text inside `PLAN_OR_INPUT` (for example "writer Wr-A ... direct injection"), next to `INJECTION_COORDINATE`. That is not the contract field.

(2) Undeclared channel. All 89 SC-A/SC-B scenarios (49 + 40) have `EXPECTED_PROCEDURAL_RESULT` = "detection channel recorded (SEMANTIC_COMPARISON, E-12, BOTH or NEITHER)". 56 of them have `EXPECTED_GROUP_VERDICT` = "PASS if the observed outcome and channel equal the declared expectation". Yet no field declares an expected channel. V2.1 10.6 line 556 requires the channel expectation "to be declared per scenario before the first governing run". As written, the scan verdict cannot be evaluated deterministically.

(3) Conditionals without a rule. 45 SC-A scenarios (Wr-A/D/E/F/G at X0..X4, plus the -EV variants at X1..X4) have `EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS` = "S-2 or S-3 difference; E-12 phase C FAIL as well if the event is delivered" with `CONDITIONAL_EXPECTATION_RULE` = NONE. The md's own section 3 (line 35) says a conditional expectation is allowed only when a declared rule resolves it offline. I count 47 control-result conditionals with no rule; the finding says 51. The difference is 2 borderline texts that are not real conditionals (in E6 and PR-FRESH), plus the count method; it does not change the substance. 64 `EXPECTED_GROUP_VERDICT` values are conditional with the rule field NONE (SC-A 45, SC-B 11, WU 6, EA1 1, EA2 1), which matches the finding exactly. The WU and EA verdict texts are closer to pass criteria than to expectations, but the 45 SC-A control-result conditionals clearly break section 3.

(4) EA2. EA2-DEFERRED-EVENTS (JSON line 2209) declares `EXPECTED_PRODUCT_OUTCOME` = "O3 SUCCESS" unconditionally, with verdict "PASS if zero events; CHARACTERIZED_DIFFERENT otherwise". Per V2.1 14.7, A-2 false means write events on protected objects after V0. Any such event before V1 is `EVT_C`, which triggers 17.2 row 7 = O7. So O3 is conditional on A-2 holding. 17.2 also says an evaluator defect is detected against the scenario's declared expected outcome, so an unconditional O3 would misflag an A-2 characterization as a mismatch.

Side observation, outside this finding: WR-*-X0 claims "E-12 phase C FAIL as well if the event is delivered". V2.1 10.6 says X0 boundary events are logged and not adjudicated (NG-19b), which strengthens the case that the channel and events expectations need their own governed fields.

Severity: MAJOR. The artifact is DRAFT, but these are required fields of the governing schema and they must exist before CANDIDATE_FOR_SEALING or seal. The fix as stated is appropriate:
- add `PURPOSE`, `INJECTIONS` (writer, variant, position) and per-phase `EXPECTED_EVENTS` / `EXPECTED_DETECTION_CHANNEL`;
- move each conditional into a `CONDITIONAL_EXPECTATION_RULE` that names its offline resolution source;
- make the EA2 product outcome conditional (O3 if no phase-C `EVT_C`, O7 otherwise).

   - Lines 35-39 build a ResultBuffer of TypedValue(DxfCode.Text, string) entries, each a Substring of at most 255 UTF-16 code units.
   - Read (lines 79-88) concatenates only the Text entries, silently ignores every other type code, and returns null when the result is empty.

   The .NET API gives no access to raw bytes. It only exposes typed values holding UTF-16 strings, so 'raw stored bytes' is not a defined observable.

3. **What is left undefined.** The spec gives no mapping from the stored ResultBuffer to the B<n>: byte field. It does not say:
   - which character encoding to use (UTF-8 or UTF-16);
   - whether to encode each chunk or the concatenated string;
   - whether chunk boundaries and type codes are part of the state;
   - how to treat entries that are not Text.

4. **Why the vectors don't close the gap.** EV-19 and EV-20 (lines 109-110, and gen.py lines 121-124) feed a ready-made ASCII byte literal. They never exercise the step from ResultBuffer to bytes. So the conformance rule 'an implementation is conformant only if it reproduces every vector' does not pin that step. An implementation using UTF-8 and one using UTF-16LE would both pass every vector and still produce different digests from the same drawing.

5. **Why the digest loses state.** 'Concatenated chunk by chunk' drops the chunk boundaries. BA-08 V2 line 89 names RBD.Read as the existing reader for PAYLOAD_EXACT, and that reader also drops every entry that is not Text. As a result, two Xrecords stored differently (different chunking, or an extra non-Text entry) get the same digest. That contradicts the 'equal digests = equal state' claim that S-5 abort verification and E-08 rely on.

6. **The surrogate-pair point.** Product-written JSON is ASCII-escaped by the default System.Text.Json encoder (RackEmbedStore at RackEmbedDocument.cs:81-85 and SelectivePalletDesignStore:117-123 set no relaxed encoder). So a surrogate pair split at a 255-unit boundary is unlikely in product output. It still matters for pre-existing or foreign payloads, which layer 1 must also fingerprint. BA-06 V2 line 169 already lists 'Round-trip fidelity of the 255-UTF-16-unit Xrecord chunks (a surrogate pair split at a boundary ...)' as open. BA-05 does not take it up.

7. **Mitigating points, none of which refute it.**
   - Contract V2.1 §28.1 line 1524 uses the same 'raw stored bytes' wording. But §28 says the detailed specification must be written out as a standalone, agreed artifact, and that artifact is BA-05, so the canonical mapping is its job.
   - The contract's string rule ('exact stored text encoded as UTF-8') does not settle this, because PAYLOAD_EXACT uses the raw-bytes kind, not the string kind.
   - The finding overstates one sub-point: the general absent/null rule '~' in §2.1 partly covers a missing payload. Still, the spec does not say whether a missing Xrecord gives '~' or no record, and it does not say how an empty buffer or a buffer with no Text entries is treated (RBD.Read returns null for both).

8. **Severity.** The artifact is DRAFT and NB-3 is declared open, so this is not BLOCKING. It must be fixed before CANDIDATE_FOR_SEALING, because a normative canonical byte stream that layer 1 depends on is underdetermined. The required fix stands:
   - define PAYLOAD_EXACT as an ordered sequence of (typeCode, typed value) over the stored ResultBuffer, keeping chunk boundaries and non-Text entries;
   - optionally add a separate derived field holding the concatenated JSON as UTF-8;
   - state explicitly how an absent or empty payload is encoded;
   - remove the 'raw stored bytes' wording;
   - regenerate EV-19 and EV-20, adding at least one vector that differs only in chunking or in a non-Text entry.
